The '''2013–14 Primeira Liga''' (also known as '''Liga ZON Sagres''' for sponsorship reasons) was the 80th season of the [[Primeira Liga]], the top professional league for Portuguese [[association football]] clubs. It began on 18 August 2013 and concluded on 11 May 2014.<ref>{{cite web|title=Calendário Liga ZON Sagres Época 2013-2014|url=http://www.ligaportugal.pt/media/5678/calendario-liga_zon_sagres-20132014.pdf|work=Liga Portugal.pt|publisher=[[Portuguese League for Professional Football]] (LPFP)|access-date=15 September 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130927150535/http://www.ligaportugal.pt/media/5678/calendario-liga_zon_sagres-20132014.pdf|archive-date=2013-09-27|url-status=dead}}</ref> Sixteen teams contested the league, fourteen of which took part in the [[2012–13 Primeira Liga|previous season]] and two of which were promoted from the [[2012–13 Segunda Liga|Segunda Liga]]. On 20 April 2014, [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] won the Primeira Liga for a record 33rd time with a 2–0 victory over [[S.C. Olhanense|Olhanense]], with two matches to spare.

==Relegation play-offs==
[[F.C. Paços de Ferreira|Paços de Ferreira]], who finished 15th, faced [[C.D. Aves|Desportivo das Aves]], the fourth-placed side of the [[2013–14 Segunda Liga]] (third-placed among non-reserve teams) for a two-legged play-off to decide the 18th team to compete in the expanded [[2014–15 Primeira Liga]]. Paços de Ferreira defeated Desportivo das Aves 3–1 on aggregate to secure their presence in the next Primeira Liga season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Playoff entre P. Ferreira e Aves com datas marcadas|trans-title=Playoff between P. Ferreira and Aves with confirmed dates|url=http://www.record.xl.pt/Futebol/Nacional/1a_liga/interior.aspx?content_id=882746|publisher=Record|language=pt|date=12 May 2014|access-date=15 May 2014|archive-date=17 May 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140517152648/http://www.record.xl.pt/Futebol/Nacional/1a_liga/interior.aspx?content_id=882746|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Television==
This was the first season that [[Sport TV]] did not broadcast any Benfica home matches. The club decided not to renew with rightsholders Olivedesportos and instead broadcast their home matches on their own channel, [[Benfica TV]].

[[RTP Internacional]] and [[RTP África]] broadcast one match per week, via satellite.
